name: X-linked Thrombocytopenia with Absent Radii
aliases: X-linked thrombocytopenia and absent radii syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Thrombocytopenia with Absent Radii

criteria.description: Bilateral absence of the radius bones confirmed by radiographic imaging
Persistent thrombocytopenia with platelet counts typically below 50,000/µL
Pathogenic mutation in the WAS gene identified by genetic testing
Clinical history of mucocutaneous bleeding or easy bruising
Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of bilateral absent radii, thrombocytopenia, and a pathogenic WAS gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by genetic testing; clinical features support diagnosis.

laboratory: Severe thrombocytopenia with normal platelet size or small platelets
imaging: Radiographs showing bilateral absence of radius bones
Possible mild skeletal deformities of upper limbs
other: Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance
Clinical bleeding tendency disproportionate to platelet count

distinguishingFeatures: Absent radii with presence of thumbs

redFlags: Severe bleeding episodes including intracranial hemorrhage
Family history of early male infant deaths or bleeding disorders
references: Nurden AT. Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome: clinical and laboratory features, pathogenesis, and treatment. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2015;2015:1-7.
Orphanet: X-linked thrombocytopenia with absent radii. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
